newsitem.title: ESTONIA: DEALERS EXPECT STRONG INTEREST IN VOUCHERS.
newsitem.headline: DEALERS EXPECT STRONG INTEREST IN VOUCHERS.

text.p: Strong buying interest in privatisation vouchers is expected on the free market of the Estonian stock exchange from Monday with the sale of stakes in two important companies, dealers said.
"Especially with the sale of the stakes in Eesti Gaas and Hotel Olympia, there will be big buying interest," one free market trader said.
"Investors have been positioning themselves for these offers for some time, so vouchers should be well traded today," another trader said.

Privatisation vouchers, which are traded on the free market of the Tallinn stock exchange, were issued as compensation for unreturned nationalised property and for the number of years worked by individuals.
AT 0800 GMT vouchers were trading at 0.315/0.334 kroons compared to Friday's close of 0.316 kroons.
"I would not be surprised to see the price reach 0.40 kroons, but the securities will be fighting the general market direction," another dealer added.
Stakes in three companies go on sale for vouchers from June 30, the privatisation agency said.
"The sale of the shares started today and will last until July 18," Marko Kadnik, pokesman of the agency, told Reuters.

A 12.33 percent stake in Eesti Gaas, the national natural gas distribution company, 25.05 percent of Hotel Olympia, one of the largest hotels in Tallinn, and a 24 percent holding in Esmeta, a steel reseller, are on offer.
